contract: C10, docs/protocol.md. The receiver (stage 2), the relay (stage 3) and the daemon (stage 4) check their code against these vectors. Every value is a sample. Since board ab-v16.30 the vectors hold the per-scope rules (the scope arg of tabs.create and windows.create, the kind scope, bridge.tabScope, the allowlist line with lists and scopes): the receiver meets them from part 1a (board ab-v16.31) on, the relay from part 2 (board ab-v16.35) on. Since board ab-v16.41 they also hold the orphan-tabs rules (the op bridge.tabScopes, the error no list for this scope, the window rule of the removal queue, the receiver's close of tabs.remove by Target.closeTarget, and TOMBSTONE_MS, RESTORE_MAX_MS and REMOVAL_WAIT_MS), which the receiver meets from part 1a on and the relay from part 2 on. Since board ab-v16.70 they also hold the daemon's own ops (daemonOps, pointerConstants, pointerWorld, pointerVectors, and the bad requests b49 and b50 of a daemon. op at the receiver): the daemon meets them from agentwatch task age-0kh.28 on, the relay from board ab-v16.71 on; the receiver only answers unknown op to a daemon. op.
allowlistNote: The union of the lists of the receiver's last applied set_scopes (C4, C5): contentDetails is checked against it (any list, C10).
setScopesNote: The receiver's last applied set_scopes of the samples (C4, C5): scope my-repo has list md, scope md-gone has no list (a session that ended), and so has every scope that it does not name. allowlist is the union of its lists.
scopeNote: The scope of the samples: a scope of C11, the second arg of tabs.create and windows.create.

kinds.id: an integer of 0 or more: a tab, window or download id
kinds.string: a string that is not empty
kinds.method: a CDP method of debugger.sendCommand: a string that is not empty; of the Target domain only the methods of targetMethods (review-22 B1: no Target.createTarget, which can open Chrome's New Tab page)
kinds.target: {"tabId": <id>} or {"tabId": <id>, "sessionId": "<child session>"}, with no other key; tabId is 0 or more
kinds.scope: a string that matches C11's scope pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$
kinds.newTab: an object with url (about:blank) and at most active (boolean), windowId and index (ids)
kinds.newWindow: an object with url (about:blank, a string) and at most focused (boolean), left, top, width, height (integers) and state; no tabId
kinds.windowUpdate: an object with at least one of left, top, width, height, state and focused, and no other key
kinds.contentDetails: exactly primaryPattern (<scheme>://<host>/* or <scheme>://<host>:<port>/*, scheme http, https or *, host covered by the allowlist, with or without *.) and setting (allow or block)

newUrl: about:blank: a new tab or window makes no request before its scope rule is in force
targetMethodsNote: The Target methods that the relay sends to Chrome through debugger.sendCommand (C11, where each call goes): the kind method allows these and no other Target method.

pointerNote: C10, the daemon's own ops (board ab-v16.70; the agent pointer design, agent-browser docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-agent-pointer-move-design.md, sections 2 and 4). The daemon (agentwatch task age-0kh.28) and the relay (board ab-v16.71) check their code against these vectors; the receiver never gets a daemon. op. Each vector gives the daemon's state (world: the keys that differ from pointerWorld; each key replaces the whole default value), the relay's request, the daemon's answer (res; null: no answer), whether the daemon reads the pointer (read: the getmouselocation before the play, or the read of daemon.pointerAt), and the lines that it plays on xdotool's standard input (script; null: no play starts). The world: xvfb, the running Xvfb's size (null: no unit Xvfb, also on the Mac); xdotool, whether the daemon finds it; xCall, whether another X call of the daemon runs; liveView, null (no live view) or its current views and the ms since the operator's last live-view input (lastInputMs; null: none yet); started, the plays (paths) and the reads that started in the last second; now, the daemon's CLOCK_MONOTONIC ms at the checks; pointer, the position that the read gives (null: the read fails or does not end in POINTER_READ_MS); playAt, the clock when the play would start (after the read); play, how the script ends: {end: the position that its getmouselocation reads}, fails (an exit code that is not 0), timeout (at the path's total time plus POINTER_KILL_MS), or a kill (operatorInput, unitStop, linkChange, relayEnd, daemonStop). A sleep line gives dt in seconds; the tests compare it as a number.

windowRuleNote: C10, removals and the last window (board ab-v16.41): one item of the receiver's removal queue. open: the tab ids of its tabs.query; pending: the tabs with a pending close (a close is pending from the moment its item starts it, for the receiver's close from the moment it joins the tab's chain, for a client's Page.close from its send, until the tab's tabs.onRemoved, or until it fails and the tab stays, after the fallback too and, when the receiver sent a Target.closeTarget command, only after that command also answered; a late answer counts as any answer); closes: the tabs that the item closes. guard: the receiver first opens an about:blank tab (not active, in no scope) in the window of the item's last tab, because no tab stays open other than the item's tabs and the pending ones.

windowRule.note: The browser's only tab (board ab-v16.39, case F: without the guard Chromium ended).
Two removals of the browser's only two tabs, one item at a time (review-48 X2b): the first item sees tab 9 stay ...
... and the second item, after tab 7's tabs.onRemoved, sees only tab 9.

Board ab-v16.43: tab 7's Page.close waits for its beforeunload dialog past REMOVAL_WAIT_MS, so tab 7 is still open but pending. The item that closes tab 9 counts tab 7 as closed: a later accept of the dialog then closes no last window.
A pending close and the operator's tab 3 (no scope): tab 3 stays open.

A later item closes a pending tab again (review-17 M1): tab 7's Page.close is held by its dialog, tab 7 is now the only open tab, and the sweep closes it by the receiver's close. No tab stays open other than the item's own tab, so the guard opens about:blank first.
The sweep closes the two tabs of an ended scope; the operator's tab 3 stays.
The sweep closes every open tab: one about:blank first.
